findings.source_passage: Her porch was bright with the bought luxury of star-shine; the wicker of the settee squeaked fashionably as she turned toward him and he kissed her curious and lovely mouth.
findings.source_locator: paragraph ending 'above the hot struggles of the poor' — the sentences immediately preceding the 'gleaming like silver' image
findings.why_it_matters: The 'bought luxury of star-shine' is a signature Fitzgerald image that sets up the 'gleaming like silver' keystone; its loss thins the thematic run-up to the Daisy-as-silver line.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'Her porch was bright with the bought luxury of star-shine...' sentence before the 'she had caught a cold' line.

findings.source_passage: On the last afternoon before he went abroad, he sat with Daisy in his arms for a long, silent time. ... They had never been closer in their month of love...
findings.source_locator: paragraph between Gatsby's 'better time telling her' speech and 'He did extraordinarily well in the war.'
findings.why_it_matters: This entire elegiac paragraph — one of the tenderest prose passages in the novel, critically engaged as the closing memory between Gatsby and Daisy — is cut whole, removing the emotional pivot between the love affair and the war.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'On the last afternoon before he went abroad...' paragraph at or near full length.

findings.source_passage: Just as Daisy's house had always seemed to him more mysterious and gay than other houses, so his idea of the city itself, even though she was gone from it, was pervaded with a melancholy beauty.
findings.source_locator: Louisville return sequence, between 'footsteps had clicked together' and 'He left feeling that if he had searched harder'
findings.why_it_matters: The Louisville passage is a signature set-piece of Gatsby's class-consciousness and melancholy; cutting 'melancholy beauty' and the white-car detail flattens a signature-tagged sequence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'melancholy beauty' sentence and the 'out-of-the-way places ... her white car' clause.

findings.source_passage: He felt their presence all about the house, pervading the air with the shades and echoes of still vibrant emotions.
findings.source_locator: end of the 'She was the first nice girl' paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: Closes the barbed-wire paragraph with characteristic Fitzgerald cadence; its loss clips the rhythm of a signature-tagged block.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the closing sentence to preserve the paragraph's cadence.

findings.source_passage: the last one of Gatsby's former servants
findings.source_locator: gardener's appearance at the foot of the steps
findings.why_it_matters: Small but telling detail of Gatsby's abandonment; drafting it out flattens atmosphere before the pool scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the appositive identifying the gardener.

summary: Three medium-severity cuts (the 'bought luxury of star-shine' image, the entire 'last afternoon before he went abroad' paragraph, and the Louisville 'melancholy beauty' sentences) flatten signature-tagged material and together trigger regeneration.
